answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent's reputation to a scarce, verifiable history instead of a fresh identity. A newcomer starts with no signal at all, while an established agent carries a relic of past work — completed tasks, peer attestations, and settled payments that cannot be faked cheaply. A sybil farm can spawn thousands of sable clones, but none inherits that earned history, so the network simply trusts proven agents more and prices new ones accordingly.
